column3: Frames painful punishment alongside the deliberate exchange of faith for disbelief.
The resolved channel places the focus within objections to changed revelation and accusations of fabrication.
Offers the positive counterpart: uncorrupted faith is joined to security and being guided.
Immediately identifies denial of Allah's signs with fabrication, extending the focus's stated group.
The resolved channel contrasts the focus with revelation as truth, steadiness, guidance, and good news for believers.
Distinguishes the caller's responsible method from Allah's knowledge of the straying and guided.
Characterizes persistent disbelief as a settled refusal of faith.
The resolved channel supplies the immediately preceding accusation about the message's human source.
Joins guidance, rejection of signs, and painful punishment in a close parallel formulation.
Shares the punishment phrase but concerns mockery of charitable believers rather than signs or guidance.
Provides a compact positive pairing of guidance with believers.
Shows painful punishment accompanying a corrupt exchange involving Allah's covenant, a broader parallel to rejected divine claims.
Connects no guidance with turning away after faith and manifest proofs, sharpening culpable reversal.
Pairs prior guidance with disbelief in Allah's signs and punishment, closely paralleling the focus.
Presents guidance into faith as Allah's gift rather than a human achievement, with sincerity at stake.
Links concealment of revealed scripture to painful punishment, adding a form of obstructing divine disclosure.
Adds a case where divine non-guidance is associated with persistent transgression despite intercession.
Shares only the punishment outcome; its conduct is boastfulness and seeking unearned praise.
Shows that prophetic and scriptural provision does not make guidance the automatic outcome for all.
States the inverse relation directly: believers affirm their Lord's signs.
Adds obedience and response to the messenger as a human-side route associated with guidance.
Adds an inward-capacity reading: guidance opens receptivity, while nonbelief is paired with constriction.
Emphasizes the unfailing force of guidance once Allah guides, without addressing sign-denial.
Links rejection of signs and covenant-breaking to sealed hearts and sparse belief.
Sets guidance within two disclosed paths, preserving a choice-facing dimension.
Contrasts Allah's guidance with a chosen object unable to speak or guide a way.
Connects following the messenger with hoped-for guidance, but remains a broad positive counterpart.
Presents faith and righteous action as associated with further guidance from the Lord.
Preserves a contrary claim: inherited tracks are called guidance without their destination being tested.
Extends the punitive side to refusal of the Hereafter, though it lacks the focus's sign-and-guidance wording.
Applies divine non-guidance to treacherous plotting, a distinct and indirect case.
Within the same surah, directly pairs concern for others' guidance with Allah's non-guidance of those left astray.
Shows reliance on anticipated divine guidance when no visible route is yet apparent.
Concerns persecution of believers and its punishment, not the focus's refusal of signs.
Pairs clear signs with Allah guiding whom He wills, supporting both disclosure and divine agency.
Adds disbelief in Allah's signs and the meeting with Him as grounds for painful punishment.
Supplies a contrary model of a ruler monopolizing the claim to show a right way.
Links denial of Allah's signs to violent rejection of prophetic and just testimony, with painful punishment.
Interprets refusal to answer revelation as following desire and joins that with divine non-guidance of wrongdoers.
Addresses speculation about angels and denial of the Hereafter, without a direct guidance relation.
Presents guidance toward the Lord as producing reverent self-restraint, a positive causal sequence.
Shares a punitive theme but concerns slander against believing women.
Identifies the Qur'an itself as guiding to the most upright course, a positive counterpart to rejecting signs.
Does not materially address belief in signs, guidance, or the focus's punitive relation.
Attributes ongoing guidance to the Creator, reinforcing divine source without the refusal context.
Shares the same-surah punishment phrase but contributes no clear sign or guidance dimension.
Shows Allah guiding responsive followers through revelation along paths of peace and a straight path.
Adds an inward condition of disease and escalation associated with lying and punishment.
Attributes future guidance to the Creator, countering inherited orientation in the nearby contrary reading.
Shows refusal persisting until painful punishment is seen, adding delayed recognition after rejection.
Shows a revealed book functioning as guidance and directing exclusive reliance on Allah.
Directly questions refusal of faith but supplies little further interpretive detail.
Offers following guided, non-compensated messengers as a limited criterion for human guidance.
Shares only the painful-punishment outcome for prior wrongdoing.
Associates faith, worship, and fear of Allah with hoped-for guidance, but only indirectly.
Shares a punishment formula but concerns harming the messenger rather than denial of signs.
Establishes the Book's guiding role for the God-conscious, a general positive counterpart.
Contains punishment alone without a useful relation to the focus.
Presents the granted Book as a means by which its recipients may be guided.
Within the same surah, adds deceptive beautification of deeds and punishment as a historical backdrop for refusal.
Contrasts Allah's guidance with Pharaoh's leadership, explicitly judged as leading astray rather than guiding.
Joins denial of signs, denial of the Hereafter, and false equivalencing of the Lord.
Associates divine non-guidance with falsehood, disbelief, and obscuring direct devotion through intermediaries.
Reiterates the irredeemability of punishment for disbelief without adding guidance or signs.
Shows one revealed discourse yielding opposite receptivity, with guidance and loss both attributed to Allah.
Shares a punishment formula but concerns spreading indecency among believers.
Presents guidance together with reminder for people of understanding, adding the role of renewed attention.
Provides a general precedent of unbelievers tasting the consequence of their affair.
Concerns confusion produced in a specific inquiry and a prospective claim to guidance.
Links active striving against Allah's signs to painful punishment.
States guidance as belonging to Allah, directly reinforcing the focus's divine agency.
Adds a doctrinal form of disbelief followed by warning of painful punishment.
Uses guidance for a recognition test in a courtly narrative, only indirectly related.
Closely depicts hearing Allah's signs, then persisting arrogantly, followed by painful punishment.
Links unknowing desire-following with being left astray and without a helper, adding a mechanism of misguidance.
Shares disbelief and painful punishment but focuses on the impossibility of ransom after death.
Pairs the accusation of fabrication with truth-bearing warning intended to open guidance.
Warns of a painful day in a call to exclusive worship, without a direct guidance or sign-rejection link.
Relates limited knowledge and desire to losing the way, while Allah knows both the straying and guided.
Is only an isolated designation of painful punishment.
Pairs evidences, guidance, and mercy for those with certainty, adding receptive perception.
Warns that opposition to the messenger's command can bring trial or painful punishment.
Presents a disclosed path while preserving divergent grateful and ungrateful responses.
Adds the gap between verbal profession and believing hearts, alongside manipulation of words.
Shows scripture and criterion given so that recipients may be guided, a repeated general pattern.
Contrasts faithful action and arrogant refusal through recompense and painful punishment.
Records rival communal claims to guidance, but its corrective focus is indirect here.
Uses belief in Allah and the messenger within a legal expiation, with a general warning for disbelievers.
Shows guidance producing faith and rejection of associating partners, a concise receptive counterpart.
Shares painful punishment for disbelievers but concerns speech etiquette rather than signs or guidance.
Frames refusal to answer Allah's caller as manifest error and lack of protection.
Presents revelation as exhortation, inward healing, guidance, and mercy for believers.
Names unperceived corruption without a material link to the focus.
Shows a detailed, knowledgeable Book becoming guidance and mercy for believers.
Affirms Allah's knowledge without a clear guidance, sign, or response relation.
Shows a human invitation to a straight path grounded in claimed knowledge, a limited secondary analogy.
Only asks about hastening punishment.
Contrasts Allah's guidance to truth with alleged guides that themselves require guidance.
Does not materially relate to belief in signs, guidance, or punishment in the focus.
Shows objects unable to answer a call to guidance, reinforcing the contrast between real and incapable guidance.
Pairs disbelief and denial of Allah's signs with an enduring punitive outcome.
Names clear signs and frames their rejection as defiant transgression.
Identifies Allah's guidance as guidance in the decisive sense, clarifying the source claim in the focus.
Links concealing clear proofs and guidance with divine rejection, adding obstruction of disclosed guidance.
Presents Allah as guiding believers through disputed truth, a positive counterpart to failed belief.
Contrasts Allah's protective leading of believers with the opposing pull toward darkness.
Uses divine non-guidance for wrongdoing, extending the focus's pattern to a broader moral category.
Uses divine non-guidance for disbelief, closely parallel to the focus's result.
Distinguishes the messenger's limited role from Allah's act of guiding whom He wills.
Directly confronts disbelief in Allah's signs while their evidentiary force is witnessed.
Directly questions obstructing Allah's way while disbelieving His signs.
Joins exposure to Allah's signs with holding fast and being guided to a straight path.
States that none can guide one Allah has left astray, reinforcing the focus's agency claim.
Describes vacillation and repeats that no way can be found for one Allah leaves astray.
Applies divine non-guidance to wrongdoing in a communal loyalty dispute.
Uses the exact category of disbelieving people in a statement that Allah does not guide them.
Uses divine non-guidance for defiantly disobedient people in a truth-bearing testimony setting.
Depicts repeated turning away whenever a sign from the Lord comes.
Combines veiled understanding with refusal to believe even after seeing every sign.
Shows Allah selecting whom He guides, while associating others would nullify their deeds.
Preserves the possibility that even demanded signs would not produce belief.
Connects prior refusal to believe with hearts and sight being turned away.
Pairs fabrication about Allah with divine non-guidance of wrongdoers.
Links denial of signs and arrogance toward them to a punitive destination.
Describes arrogant turning from signs and refusal to believe even when signs are seen.
Joins denial of signs and the meeting with Allah to the nullification of deeds.
States that one Allah leaves astray has no guide, with wandering left unresolved.
Links disbelief in Allah's signs to a punitive historical pattern.
Applies divine non-guidance to wrongdoing despite religious-service claims.
Uses divine non-guidance for defiantly disobedient people when rival attachments displace Allah's cause.
Links obstinate disbelief to unforgiveness and divine non-guidance of transgressors.
Applies divine non-guidance to wrongdoers in a setting of unstable religious construction.
Directly warns against becoming among those who deny Allah's signs.
States that some will not believe even if every sign comes to them.
Preserves the distinction between Allah's power over belief and compelled human belief.
Makes belief contingent on Allah's permission and associates unreason with defilement.
Contrasts personal benefit from being guided with personal loss from going astray.
States that no adviser can benefit a people if Allah wills their error.
Pairs Allah's leaving astray with His guiding those who turn toward Him.
Directly sets divine misguidance and guidance within Allah's will.
Contrasts the firm establishment of believers with the leaving astray of wrongdoers.
Within the same surah, distinguishes those Allah guided from those for whom error became due.
Within the same surah, directly presents Allah guiding and leaving astray whom He wills.
Explains the historical rejection of signs as relevant to their sending and punishment.
Defines the rightly guided as those Allah guides and denies protectors to those He leaves astray.
Links denial of Allah's signs with a specified punitive consequence.
States that Allah's guidance is decisive and that one left astray has no directing guide.
Directly joins being reminded of divine signs, turning away, blocked comprehension, and never being guided.
Shows Allah increasing those already guided in guidance.
Associates repentance, belief, right action, and then guidance as a distinct sequence.
States that following divine guidance prevents straying, a direct positive converse to the focus.
Makes forgotten divine signs the ground of a corresponding exclusion, clarifying response to signs.
Links recognition of revealed truth and belief to Allah guiding believers to a straight path.
Depicts denial visibly appearing when clear signs are recited, with punishment threatened.
Presents Allah as guiding whom He wills to His light, adding a major positive guidance image.
States that Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path after clear signs are sent down.
Depicts denial of signs despite inward certainty, through wrongdoing and arrogance.
Uses inability to guide those blind to error as a secondary parallel to non-guidance.
Directly distinguishes the messenger's desire to guide from Allah's guidance of whom He wills.
Pairs belief in revelation with the claim that only disbelievers reject Allah's signs.
Shows striving toward Allah met with guidance to His ways, a positive response-side counterpart.
Uses inability to guide those blind from error as a parallel limit on human guidance.
Directly joins being reminded of Allah's signs and turning away from them.
Presents revealed knowledge as guidance to a path leading to Allah.
Contrasts Allah's leaving astray and guiding with the fair-seeming of corrupt action.
Uses divine non-guidance for one who is both transgressing and habitually false.
States that one Allah leaves astray has no guide.
Links divine misguidance with persistent transgression and doubt.
Depicts disputing Allah's signs without authority as arrogance followed by a sealed heart.
Shows that guidance can be offered while blindness is deliberately preferred.
Presents Allah as choosing and guiding to Himself those who turn back.
States that one Allah leaves astray has no protecting ally afterward.
States that one Allah leaves astray has no path back.
Links taking desire as a god with being left astray knowingly and having perception sealed.
Pairs arrogance and denial of signs with a humiliating punitive outcome.
Shows Allah increasing guidance and God-consciousness for those who are guided.
Links turning back after guidance has become clear with satanic enticement and false hope.
Adds an inward counterpart: faith made beloved and disbelief made hateful.
Shows deviation followed by hearts being turned away, and names divine non-guidance of transgressors.
Combines fabrication about Allah with divine non-guidance of wrongdoers.
Uses divine non-guidance for wrongdoers who bear scripture without carrying it.
Associates belief in Allah with Allah guiding the heart.
Presents revelation as bringing believers from darkness into light.
Directly states that Allah leaves astray and guides whom He wills.
Adds a concise personal attribution of guidance to Allah.
